key_insight: VecTile uses passive silicone nubs to turn normal and shear forces into distinguishable pressure patterns, enabling low-cost, flexible three-axis tactile sensing.
engineering_relevance: The 6 mm-thin sensor gives robots contact-force feedback for grasp stability and manipulation at a complete-system cost below $35 for a 4×4 array.
method: Combine a piezoresistive layer with silicone nubs that mechanically encode force direction.
Validate the sensing mechanism with finite element analysis and hardware experiments.
Calibrate force readings and test curved operation and robotic manipulation.
evidence_signal: Controlled single-taxel tests over 1–5 N normal force and up to 1.5 N shear force achieved RMSEs of 0.39 N and 0.16 N, respectively; demonstrations included balloon-puncture prevention and improved Diffusion Policy-guided plug insertion.
watch_item: Reported force errors come from controlled single-taxel tests, so they do not establish full-array accuracy under complex simultaneous contacts.
paper_title: VecTile: A Low-Cost Flexible Tactile Array for 3-DoF Force Sensing
